recent_lessons.lesson: HBR: AI-tool edges commoditize as adoption saturates — the residual claimants are org structure and human judgment, not the model layer; the AI trade is repricing from silicon to systems (services/power/platforms over picks-and-shovels).

Fri Jul 17 pre-open — the AI trade is repricing from silicon to systems, and yesterday's unwind did not stabilize: KOSPI -6.37%, Taiwan -6.47%, Nikkei -4.03%, Shenzhen -5.4%, with memory/storage taking the worst of it (SNDK -12.6%, STX -10.0%, WDC -9.2%, MRVL -8.7%, MU -5.7%). US futures follow (NASDAQ F -1.85%), VIX +9.8% to 18.37, gold $4,002, 10Y down to 4.529%, copper -1.96%. Semis are described as 'on the verge of a bear market.' Two days ago the tape ignored a record TSMC print; today it is selling the whole complex. That sequence — best-possible fundamentals cannot hold a bid, then the bid leaves entirely — is the signature of capex enthusiasm converting into ROI scrutiny, not of a growth scare. CNBC's own framing is the trade: 'services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels,' with Cramer demanding 'cold hard proof that AI is paying off.' The academic tape says the same thing from the other end: an AI cover-letter tool on a 5.5M-application platform lifted callbacks 50% and decayed to ZERO edge within two months as adoption spread (HBR Research Roundup, 07-16), and HBS's automation-cliff math shows AI gains reprice discontinuously rather than on a glide path (aiinstitute.hbs.edu, 07-16). WOLF read: do not fade this as an oversold bounce setup on the picks-and-shovels names — the marginal buyer is already fully invested and the story is rotating, not dipping. The durable asset is never the tool; it is the structure the tool runs inside. Position accordingly: the names that monetize AI throughput (services, platforms, power) are where the bid migrates, and any AI-derived edge you can name is on a two-month decay clock unless it is structurally fenced. Cross-currents to respect: crude +2.0% to $80.54 on expanded US strikes (Iran civilian infrastructure, now Syria and Bahrain) and mortgage rates at 2026 highs with builders cutting prices across 10 metros — the war bid and the housing crack are independent of the AI trade and both deserve their own position structures.

HBR/HBS: AI-derived edges mean-revert on adoption - an AI cover-letter tool lifted callbacks 50% then decayed to ZERO within two months as adoption spread (5.5M applications, Cui/Dias/Ye, HBR 7/16); employers reweighted to work history. Pairs with HBS 'automation cliffs' (Gu/Li/Zhu): AI gains do NOT price smoothly - once AI crosses a performance threshold, equilibrium jumps abruptly to AI-only, so labor displacement and margin repricing arrive as discontinuities, not glide paths. Trade the structure, not the tool: today's tape confirms (KOSPI -6.4%, TWN -6.5%, memory SNDK -12.6/STX -10.0/WDC -9.2, VIX +9.8%) with CNBC rotating to 'services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels.'

A 12-point swing in one index in two sessions is not rotation, it's forced positioning unwinding through a thin book. The tell is the divergence between fundamentals and price: TSMC printed a record quarter (Q2 profit +77%, +$100B additional Arizona commitment) and the tape still sold the complex — when the best possible print can't hold a bid, the marginal buyer is already fully invested ('expectations are now exceptionally high'). Confirming: margin debt at levels seen at past market tops (CNBC), momentum 'hit a wall after the biggest unwind since 2001' (MarketWatch), IBM -25% leaving employees down $400M on company stock, SpaceX through its IPO price for the first time. The macro cross-current is the sharpest signal: consumer prices FELL for the first time since early COVID and wholesale prices dropped, yet the 10Y rose to 4.575 and the 30Y to 5.109. Disinflation that lifts yields means the bid is leaving duration for reasons other than growth — supply, term premium, or a Fed chair (Warsh) who 'has said nothing to signal he wants to get in front of the AI trade' (Sahm). WOLF POSTURE: leverage down, not direction on. In a dispersion regime with margin debt at top-like levels, position size is the only variable fully under our control. Do not add to AI-complex beta on strength; do not fade it on weakness. Watch Hormuz (Iran 'red line', oil 79.11, US reserves at a 40-year low) as the tail that converts an orderly unwind into a correlated one — refiners are the asymmetric hedge, not the index.
